findings.title: Redefining `self.downsize` overwrites the 4-5 argument version in Ruby
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` on line 149 immediately overwrites `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined on line 145. Any existing caller passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` (or `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`) will now either have `max_height` treated as `opts` (causing a `TypeError: no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed on an Integer) or raise an `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)`.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and server settings
findings.body: Replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10 MB) disables the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` check on the client for non-image attachments (which are not downsized by the server), and also blocks uploads when an administrator has configured `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` higher than 10 MB.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing fails because `gifsicle --resize-fit` does not accept percentage dimensions
findings.body: When a GIF is uploaded and `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled, `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `gifsicle`'s `--resize-fit` option requires `WxH` pixel dimensions (unlike `--scale`), so `gifsicle` fails with a non-zero exit status on every iteration and the loop runs 5 times without downsizing the GIF.
